methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $20M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Amperon is a Series B–stage infrastructure and logistics company founded by Sean Kelly. The company has raised $20M to date. The comparable universe for this sector includes no identified public or private peers with sufficient data availability to support a formal peer multiple analysis.

Given data constraints, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology. Using total capital raised of $20M as a proxy for implied post-money valuation at Series A close, a 1.9x multiplier applied to Series B financing produces an implied valuation of $38M. This step-up ratio reflects typical dilution and value creation patterns observed across Series A to Series B financings in infrastructure-focused venture portfolios.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $32M to $44M, centered on $38M. The median reflects the stage-progression output directly. The range captures reasonable variance around assumed step-up multiples (1.6x to 2.2x), acknowledging uncertainty in the exact Series A post-money valuation and stage-specific market conditions. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable company benchmarks to validate sector-specific growth and margin profiles, and lack of visibility into Amperon's unit economics, customer concentration, and revenue traction relative to infrastructure-logistics peers. Completion of a peer comp set would materially improve precision around any final valuation conclusion.
